sources.entry: Tabbit - An AI-native browser that understands your context, chats with webpages, and automates tasks. ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Tabbit Browser
summary.one_liner: Tabbit is an AI-native desktop browser by Lumina Lab that chats with webpages, runs multi-step agent tasks, and supports custom Skills.
use_cases: automating multi-step web tasks with an agent
research and literature review with saved papers
summarizing podcasts, videos, or long threads
reviewing pull requests from a browser
summary.what_it_does: Tabbit lets you chat with the current page, PDFs, bookmarks, screenshots, and highlighted elements by dropping them into the chat with @ mentions. Its Agent plans and runs multi-step tasks, and the page describes multiple agents (research, operator, writer, analyst) each loaded with Skills. Skills are prebuilt or user-created add-ons; the page lists many site-specific ones for video, papers, email, and chat history. Users can choose among several AI models, including GPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen and others. It also offers automatic tab organization and can import history, bookmarks, and extensions from Safari, Edge, or Chrome.
notable: Chat with webpages, PDFs, screenshots and highlights using @ mentions
Skills marketplace with site-specific automation, and a Skill Creator program
Choice of many AI models, with the active model shown in chat
Imports history, bookmarks, and extensions from Safari, Edge, or Chrome
caveats: Pro is an optional paid tier for top-tier models and frequent Agent use; free users get a weekly allowance
Linux and mobile are only on the roadmap
Page says 'Launching Early June' and lists the Skills catalog as upcoming, so availability may vary
